people.name: Valdo H. Viglielmo
people.field: Japanese literature and works of Japanese philosophy

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: He was sent to the University of Pennsylvania where he began an intensive nine-month course of study, almost exclusively in the spoken language.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: In October 1946, after his military discharge, Viglielmo transferred to Harvard University to continue his study of Japanese in the then-Far Eastern Languages Department. He received his A.B. degree

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.role: teaching English as a foreign language
relations.evidence: chose instead to go to Japan for a three-year position teaching English as a foreign language at Meiji Gakuin University in Tokyo.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: In the summer of 1951 Viglielmo returned to Harvard, receiving his M.A. degree in June 1952.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: That same year he won a Ford Foundation Fellowship for two years of graduate study in Japan, studying both at Tokyo University and the Gakushūin University.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: At Gakushūin University, Viglielmo participated in a graduate seminar on Sōseki conducted by Sōseki biographer Komiya Toyotaka.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: In the spring of 1955 his Harvard teacher, Serge Elisséeff, asked Viglielmo if he would accept an appointment as a Harvard instructor

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.role: instructor in Japanese language and literature
relations.evidence: accept an appointment as a Harvard instructor in Japanese language and literature, beginning in Fall 1955. He taught at Harvard until June 1958

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: He then entered the Harvard Ph.D. program in Japanese Literature... having completed his doctoral dissertation in December 1955 and having received his Ph.D. degree in March 1956.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: During the period from Fall 1958 until June 1960 he taught at International Christian University as well as Tokyo Women's Christian University and Tokyo University.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: In September 1960, Viglielmo received an appointment as assistant professor at Princeton University, where he taught Japanese language and literature. In January 1965, he accepted an offer

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.role: associate professorship, promoted to full professor
relations.evidence: In January 1965, he accepted an offer of an associate professorship in the then Department of Asian and Pacific Languages at the University of Hawaiʻi. Viglielmo was soon promoted to full professor and taught at the University of Hawai‘i until his retirement at the end of August 2002.

relations.subject: Valdo H. Viglielmo
relations.evidence: Viglielmo's most sustained work in modern Japanese philosophy was a collaborative effort with David A. Dilworth and Agustin Jacinto Zavala, A Sourcebook for Modern Japanese Philosophy, in 1998.
